national_raw_news.content: Vice President C P Radhakrishnan today inaugurated 9th India International Water Week 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, he stressed the precise usage of water and highlighted that it should be conserved. He underlined that Water Week is a significant platform to bring all stakeholders to deliberate upon the processing challenges of water management. He said that no single institution, sector or State can address the challenges related to water in isolation and called upon greater cooperation and a coordinated approach. Vice President further emphasised the need for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach that brings together technological innovation, sound policy, scientific knowledge, local experience and community participation. He said such cooperation must extend across administrative and geographical boundaries to ensure sustainable, equitable and effective management of water resources. Mr Radhakrishnan said that climate change is making rainfall patterns increasingly uncertain, necessitating systems capable of managing both periods of excessive rainfall and prolonged dry spells. He stressed that river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation must work together as part of an integrated approach to water management. Jal Shakti Minister C.R Patil highlighted the importance of water conservation and said that government is committed in providing safe and sufficient drinking water to every citizen in the country. He said that Water is a shared resource, and therefore, water security is also a shared responsibility. The theme of this year’s water week is Climate Resilient Water Management. The five-day international event will provide a multidisciplinary platform bringing together policymakers, global water leaders, experts, researchers, practitioners, industry, civil society and young professionals for dialogue, knowledge exchange, innovation and partnerships towards addressing emerging water challenges and advancing a water-secure and climate-resilient future.

national_raw_news.title: 26 mins ago | National 150 HM Amit Shah inaugurates National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force Heads in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States and UTs in New Delhi. The two day conference serves as a powerful platform to safeguard future generations from the menace of drugs. Heads of ANTFs from 36 States and Union Territories are attending the conference, being organised by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). Based on the theme of the United Resolve, Shared Responsibility, the conference is focussing on progress of targets assigned to State and UTs ANTFs in recently released Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-29). During the event, Union Home Minister Amit Shah also launched the new website of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). He released four Television Commercials to create awareness among people about drug abuse. Mr Shah also laid the foundation stones for the new zonal office and residential complex of the NCB in Lucknow and a new zonal office complex in Dehradun. During the conference, deliberations will also focus on identifying and adopting appropriate strategies to further strengthen the Central Government’s measures for supply reduction, demand reduction, and harm reduction. The discussions are expected to generate actionable strategies to further strengthen drug law enforcement and keep the youth of the country away from drugs. Union Home Ministry said that Central government is working in mission mode to protect the nation’s youth from the adverse effects of drug abuse. The Ministry said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has set the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, and realising this vision is not possible without building a drug-free India.

national_raw_news.title: 28 mins ago | National 302 President Droupadi Murmu to present 72nd National Film Awards in Gujarat today
national_raw_news.content: Marking a new chapter in Indian cinema, President Droupadi Murmu will present the historic 72nd National Film Awards this evening at Ekta Nagar. Instituted in 1954, these awards represent India’s highest cinematic honours, recognising artistic and technical excellence across various categories, namely Feature, Non-Feature, and Writing on Cinema. As part of a major policy initiative by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards are being held outside the national capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar brings together cinematic talent from across the country, embodying the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. The president will also honour the veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. The stage is set, and the lights are ready in the iconic Ekta Nagar as Kevadia prepares to host the historic 72nd National Film Awards for the very first time. Renowned actors, acclaimed filmmakers, and technicians from across the country have started arriving at the venue for this grand celebration of Indian cinema. The ceremony honours outstanding cinematic achievements for the year 2024. Among the major feature film announcements, Article 370 was selected for Best Feature Film, with Yami Gautam winning Best Actress for her role in the film. The Best Actor honour is shared by Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Rajkumar Periasamy earned Best Direction for Amaran, while Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. In the non-feature category, the Marathi film Bhangaar was named Best Non-Feature Film, while Director Aanand L Rai was selected for Best Direction for Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. Ravi Raj Murmu took the Best Debut Director (Non-Feature) honour for the Santhali film, Angen.

national_raw_news.title: Sikkim’s natural farming journey reflects PM Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 7 hours ago 89
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Apart from mystic lakes and snow-capped mountains, Sikkim is famous for its vast agricultural offerings not only in India but also to the world. Sikkim has been declared the 1st Organic State in 2016 and is famous for crops like large cardamom, ginger buckwheat etc. Sikkim produces around 90% of large cardamom, which is Highest Large Cardamom in India, and exported to countries like Australia and the UAE. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Beema Yojana has played a pivotal role in the natural farming scenario in Sikkim. Apart from Large Cardamom, Buckwheat is one of the crops that’s extensively harvested in Sikkim which is around 1600kg per hector. Being the 3rd largest crop and 2nd most common cereal crop in Sikkim Buckwheat has a GI Certification. With time and with firm collaboration with Govt of India, ICAR Sikkim and Department of Agriculture, Govt of Sikkim the scene of Natural Farming as well as Organic Farming is growing stronger in Sikkim.
